note:
The manifest of every external input to this tree, code and data alike. Nothing enters the tree undeclared (plan L0 step 3). Entries are pinned by URL and SHA-256, never by version range, because rule R11 applies to code for the same reason it applies to data: upstream is mutable and a resolver hides that. See MANIFEST.md for the format.

ARCHIVES DECLARE WHAT IS TAKEN OUT OF THEM. An archive's SHA-256 pins the container and says nothing about which of its members this tree reads. Every entry with `unpack` therefore carries `consumes` — `whole-tree` where the archive is compiled entire, `declared-members` where it is not — and a `members` list giving each individually-read member its own SHA-256: the licence text quoted verbatim into NOTICE, the file compared against a populated FetchContent tree, or a data member extracted into the cache because something outside Python needs a path to it. tools/fetch.py refuses an archive entry that declares neither. The rule was prompted by EGM2008, which ships seven members of which this tree reads two and deliberately does not open hsynth_WGS84.f, and it applies to every archive rather than to the one that revealed it.

entries.licence_note: TRIPLE-LICENSED, AND THE CHOICE IS RECORDED HERE BECAUSE IT HAS TO BE MADE. CALCEPH's own LICENSE: "The library is 'triple-licensed' (CeCILL-C, CeCILL-B or CeCILL), you have to choose one of the three licenses below to apply on the library." This tree chooses CeCILL-B, the BSD-like option. It is the ONLY one of the three compatible with plan §5 constraint 3: CeCILL-C is close to the GNU LGPL and CeCILL v2.1 is GPL-compatible, and tools/fetch.py's allowlist refuses both by name. Note that neither contains the string 'GPL', so the denylist this project used until 2026-09-18 would have passed them. OBLIGATIONS, heavier than BSD's and binding a FUTURE distribution rather than this tree today: CeCILL-B §5.3.4 CREDITS requires a distributor of MODIFIED software to state that it is based on CALCEPH, reproduce the intellectual-property notice, make that notice reachable from the software's interface, and mention it on a freely accessible website for as long as it is distributed. This tree links CALCEPH unmodified. The predecessor links it statically and records no choice at all, which is the situation this entry exists not to inherit.

entries.role: TAI − UTC, the leap-second table (SPEC-time §4.5, §4.7)
entries.version: through IERS Bulletin C 72, July 2026; expires 2027-06-28
entries.licence_note: IERS public product, published by the Earth Orientation Centre for unrestricted use. Not redistributed by this tree: the pin is the IERS's own URL and the hash is the identity.
entries.upstream_mutable_note: Rewritten whenever a leap second is announced. That is precisely why it is pinned: a change here is a change of one second, which is 7.5 km of along-track position at LEO, and it must be a reviewed act rather than something a re-fetch does quietly. The file also states its own expiry, which SPEC-time TIME-R-051 enforces as a refusal with exactly one named, logged escape hatch.

entries.role: IERS EOP 20 C04 — the final Earth orientation series (SPEC-eop §4.1)
entries.licence_note: IERS public product. Not redistributed: the pin is the IERS's own URL.
entries.upstream_mutable_note: THIS IS THE ARCHIVED PATH, deliberately, per plan §3.11 point 3. The live series at .../eopc04/ is revised RETROACTIVELY at an unchanged URL — three documented instances (2025-06-05, 2026-02-05, 2026-03-09), two of which rewrote historical pole coordinates for 2021-2024. The IERS archives each superseded solution at a stable path as it retires it, so pinning one records a URL and redistributes nothing. Operational runs may use the live series; they must record its identity and hash in run provenance.

entries.role: JPL DE440 planetary and lunar ephemeris, WITH the TT-TDB time ephemeris — the full-span kernel, and the only independent check of tdb_minus_tt in this tree
entries.licence_note:
SUBSTITUTED FOR de440.bsp on 2026-09-18, not added alongside it, and the substitution was verified rather than assumed: reading both DAFs' segment summaries directly, de440t.bsp carries de440.bsp's 14 segments with IDENTICAL frame, type and span, plus ONE more — target 1000000001 about centre 1000000000, the TT-TDB time ephemeris. Nothing that consumed de440.bsp loses anything.
WHY: accuracy is not the argument. At 1 microsecond of TDB-TT error, ten times any error credibly attributed to the analytic series, the Sun's geocentric position moves 30 mm and the third-body acceleration by about 3.5e-15 m/s^2, which nothing in this tree can see. The argument is that tdb_minus_tt otherwise has NO independent check anywhere, and the failure it is exposed to is not a 100 ns failure but a wrapping, unit or sign failure: 1 ms puts the Sun 30 m out and the Moon 1 m out, and that is visible everywhere.
NOTE THE HOST: de440t.bsp is published by JPL SSD, not by NAIF. NAIF's generic_kernels/spk/planets/ carries de440, de440s, de441 and de442 and NO de440t, and the obvious URL there is a 404.
Plan §5 constraint 9: changing this entry re-ran step 1's FULL testpo.440 sweep against the substituted kernel, in the step that changed it.

entries.role: EGM2008 fully normalised spherical harmonic coefficients to degree 2190, order 2159 — the field SPEC-gravity implements
entries.licence_note: NGA publishes EGM2008 for unrestricted use; the README asks that Pavlis, Holmes, Kenyon and Factor (EGU 2008) be cited, which PROVENANCE.md §4 does. Data, never linked. THE ARCHIVE ALSO CONTAINS hsynth_WGS84.f AND hsynth_WGS84.exe, a FORTRAN harmonic-synthesis program and its binary. Neither is extracted and neither was opened: plan §3.3 step 2 says this tree's recursions come from published mathematics rather than from anyone's code, and declaring the archive whole while consuming two of its seven members is what makes that claim checkable rather than merely asserted. Zeta-to-N_to2160_egm2008 (142 MB) is not extracted either; it is the geoid conversion expansion, which GRAV-Q-002 ruled out of scope.
entries.consumes_note: TWO of the archive's seven members are consumed and the other five are not opened at all, hsynth_WGS84.f and hsynth_WGS84.exe among them. An archive hash says nothing about what is taken out of an archive; the member hashes are what make that claim checkable rather than asserted.

entries.role: NGA.STND.0036 — WGS 84 normal gravity at the pole and the semi-minor axis, for GRAV-A-012's external band check
entries.licence_note: Pinned for exactly two numbers — gamma_p = 9.8321849379 m/s^2 and b = 6356752.3142 m (Table 3.6, Table 3.1) — which are the only expected values in SPEC-gravity §8 that come from outside this tree's own mathematics. Note that its GM, 3986004.418e8 m^3 s^-2, IS NUMERICALLY the TCG-compatible EGM2008 value under another name, so it cannot be refused on its value; what GRAV-F-005 refuses is taking both constants from here, since this document's semi-major axis is 6378137.0 m against EGM2008's reference radius of 6378136.3 m.

entries.role: NAIF gm_de440.tpc — the GM of every solar-system body consistent with DE440, for third-body attraction
entries.licence_note: A DE440 SPK carries NO constants — getconstantcount returns zero, which SPEC-ephemerides EPH-R-012 records — so the GMs a third-body model needs are not in the kernel that supplies the positions. This is NAIF's own text PCK carrying them, consistent with DE440 by construction. Parsed by this tree rather than read through CALCEPH, so that the parse is auditable and so that loading it cannot change what Ephemeris reports about its own kernels. Two of its values are cross-checked against TN36-1's independently pinned constants: GM_sun directly, and GM_moon through the Moon-Earth mass ratio.

Editing the reference would have compromised the only thing step 4 has to check against.

entries.role: GFZ Kp/ap/Ap and the DRAO F10.7 it redistributes — the space-weather input (SPEC-atmosphere §4.3a)
entries.licence_file: (stated in the file's own header, lines 2 and 18)
entries.licence_note: THE LICENCE OF WHAT THIS TREE CONSUMES, which is not the licence of the whole file. The file is CC BY 4.0 except the sunspot-number column SN, which is CC BY-NC 4.0 (WDC-SILSO, Royal Observatory of Belgium) and is named in licence_excluded below. Declaring the compound licence instead would have put a non-commercial term on tools/fetch.py's permissive allowlist, which is precisely what that allowlist exists to prevent. The columns mechanism makes the exclusion checkable rather than asserted: the verifier refuses if a declared column carries an excluded licence (SPEC-atmosphere ATMO-R-032, ATMO-F-016).
entries.consumes_note: A column list is to a table what a member list is to an archive: the file hash says nothing about WHICH PART of the file is read, and here the parts carry different licences.

entries.upstream_mutable_note: Extended daily AND REVISED in place: the D flag records it (2 = definitive, 1 = Kp definitive, 0 = preliminary; 34 424 + 153 + 17 = 34 594 on this snapshot). Revision is why ATMO-R-024 refuses to compare results from two snapshots even at an epoch both cover, and why §5 constraint 9 re-running every consuming gate on a manifest change is the mechanism that lets a moving input have a reproducible gate. entries.role: IAU 2012 Resolution B2 — the astronomical unit is 149 597 870 700 m EXACTLY, and is used with all time scales (SPEC-ephemerides EPH-P-2, EPH-A-003)
entries.version: adopted by the XXVIII General Assembly, Beijing, 30 August 2012
entries.licence_note: An IAU General Assembly resolution: a published standards document. Text, never linked.
entries.verify_note: OBTAINED FROM SYRTE (Observatoire de Paris), NOT FROM THE IAU, because the IAU no longer serves it. Searched 2026-09-18 and recorded so the next reader need not repeat it: https://www.iau.org/static/resolutions/IAU2012_English.pdf (404, http and https), .../IAU_2012_English.pdf (404), https://iau.org/administration/resolutions/ (404), https://www.iau.org/administration/resolutions/general_assemblies/ (404) and .../ga2012/ (404). SYRTE hosts the IERS Conventions Centre and serves the individual resolution text. That bounds the search; it does not establish that the IAU publishes no copy anywhere. THE DOCUMENT WAS READ, NOT JUST FETCHED: recommendation 1 is 'that the astronomical unit be re-defined to be a conventional unit of length equal to 149 597 870 700 m exactly', and recommendation 2 is 'that this definition of the astronomical unit be used with all time scales such as TCB, TDB, TCG, TT, etc.' The second matters here: the au carries NO time-scale dependence, unlike the GM values of PERT-A-028 where the TDB/TCB rate L_B is exactly what separates two published numbers.
